# LinkedIn Draft - 2026-09-13

RTK's 89% token reduction did not translate into lower AI coding costs in a 1,740-attempt benchmark; costs were flat to 17% higher depending on model and weighting.

Went through 40 links today. Here's what made the brief:

1. RTK reports 89% token savings, but Quesma's cost benchmarks disagree
   Stops a plausible-sounding cost optimization from being adopted on vendor-reported token counts alone.

2. Family Stitch: a shared family calendar driven entirely over SMS
   Direct adjacency to text-and-voice scheduling work — same channel, same coordination problem.

3. Rare Not Random: using token efficiency for secrets scanning
   Directly actionable improvement to secret scanning, from the Gitleaks author, with published metrics.

4. How Infisical rebuilt complex permissions without migrating to Zanzibar
   Concrete counterweight to the default 'adopt Zanzibar' advice, with the backward-compatibility constraints spelled out.

5. Rune, a native keyboard-driven Go IDE, is now open source (GPLv3)
   Editor-integrated CLI model is worth a look if you live in terminal tiles, and the licence makes it inspectable.

Full brief with all 40 researched links → https://thenightlylibrarian.com/briefs/2026-09-13
